question.text: What must you hold before you drive a motor vehicle on North Carolina public streets and highways?

answer.text: In North Carolina it is illegal to drive a motor vehicle on public streets and highways unless you hold a valid driver license; driving is a legal privilege that comes with responsibility.

teaching.text: Driving on public streets and highways is a privilege, and it starts with holding a valid driver license. Remember: no license, no driving.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In North Carolina it is illegal to drive a motor vehicle on public streets and highways unless you hold a valid driver license; driving is a legal privilege that comes with responsibility.

question.text: Besides driving, what two things are you barred from doing without a valid license?

answer.text: Without a valid license you also may not sit behind the wheel while the engine is running, or steer a vehicle while another vehicle pushes or tows it.

teaching.text: The ban reaches past driving itself: no sitting at the wheel with the engine running, and no steering a pushed or towed vehicle. Remember: engine running counts too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Without a valid license you also may not sit behind the wheel while the engine is running, or steer a vehicle while another vehicle pushes or tows it.

question.text: Who may get a regular learner permit in North Carolina?

answer.text: A regular learner permit is available to anyone who is eighteen years old or older.

teaching.text: The regular learner permit opens at eighteen years old or older. Remember: eighteen and up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A regular learner permit is available to anyone who is eighteen years old or older.

question.text: What does a learner permit let its holder drive, and when?

answer.text: A learner permit lets its holder drive the type or class of vehicle it names, but only while the permit is in the holder's possession.

teaching.text: The permit covers only the vehicle type or class it names, and only while you have it with you. Remember: named vehicle, permit in pocket.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A learner permit lets its holder drive the type or class of vehicle it names, but only while the permit is in the holder's possession.

question.text: Who must ride with a permit holder driving on the highway, and where do they sit?

answer.text: When a permit holder drives on the highway, a person licensed for that vehicle must ride in the seat beside them.

teaching.text: On the highway, a person licensed for that vehicle rides in the seat right beside the permit holder. Remember: licensed rider sits beside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a permit holder drives on the highway, a person licensed for that vehicle must ride in the seat beside them.

question.text: Who must accompany a learner permit holder while driving on the highways?

answer.text: While driving a motor vehicle on the highways, a learner permit holder must be accompanied by a person licensed to operate that vehicle who is seated beside the permit holder.

teaching.text: The permit holder always needs a licensed companion alongside, while a licensed driver may drive alone. Remember: Licensed companion seated beside you.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While driving a motor vehicle on the highways, a learner permit holder must be accompanied by a person licensed to operate that vehicle who is seated beside the permit holder.

question.text: Which tests must you pass to get a learner permit?

answer.text: To get a learner permit you must pass a vision check, a traffic signs test and a test on motor vehicle laws.

teaching.text: A learner permit takes three passes: a vision check, a traffic signs test and a motor vehicle laws test. Remember: eyes, signs, laws.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To get a learner permit you must pass a vision check, a traffic signs test and a test on motor vehicle laws.

question.text: What can an applicant for an original driver license be tested on?

answer.text: Applicants for any original driver license may be tested on vision, motor vehicle law knowledge, traffic signs, and driving skill in an on-road test.

teaching.text: An original license can test vision, law knowledge, traffic signs and on-road driving skill. Remember: eyes, laws, signs, road.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants for any original driver license may be tested on vision, motor vehicle law knowledge, traffic signs, and driving skill in an on-road test.

question.text: Can a strong score on one license test make up for a failed one?

answer.text: Every driver license test is scored on its own, so you must pass each one separately.

teaching.text: Scores are never averaged; every test must be passed on its own. Remember: pass each test alone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every driver license test is scored on its own, so you must pass each one separately.

question.text: Which test can an original license require that a learner permit does not?

answer.text: The learner permit tests are vision, signs and motor vehicle law knowledge, while an original license can also require the on-road driving skill test.

teaching.text: The on-road driving skill test is the one an original license can add on top of the permit tests. Remember: road test is extra.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The learner permit tests are vision, signs and motor vehicle law knowledge, while an original license can also require the on-road driving skill test.

question.text: What must you do with each sign on the traffic signs test?

answer.text: On the signs test you must recognize each traffic sign by its color and shape and say what it means; every sign on that test appears in the handbook.

teaching.text: Recognize each sign by color and shape and give its meaning; every sign on the test is in the handbook. Remember: color, shape, meaning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On the signs test you must recognize each traffic sign by its color and shape and say what it means; every sign on that test appears in the handbook.

question.text: What does the knowledge test cover, and what help is offered to weak readers?

answer.text: The knowledge test covers traffic laws and safe driving practices, and an audio version can be requested by applicants who struggle with reading.

teaching.text: The knowledge test is about traffic laws and safe driving practices, and an audio version can be requested. Remember: laws, safety, audio option.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The knowledge test covers traffic laws and safe driving practices, and an audio version can be requested by applicants who struggle with reading.

question.text: How is the signs test different from the knowledge test?

answer.text: The signs test and the knowledge test are not the same test: the signs test asks you to identify signs by color and shape and give their meaning, while the knowledge test covers traffic laws and safe driving practices.

teaching.text: The signs test is about recognizing signs, and the knowledge test is about laws and safe practices. Remember: signs look, knowledge rules.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The signs test and the knowledge test are not the same test: the signs test asks you to identify signs by color and shape and give their meaning, while the knowledge test covers traffic laws and safe driving practices.

question.text: When is your vision checked during licensing?

answer.text: Your vision is checked whenever you apply in person, whether for a learner permit, an original license or a renewal.

teaching.text: Every in-person application includes a vision check, whether for a permit, a first license or a renewal. Remember: every in-person visit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Your vision is checked whenever you apply in person, whether for a learner permit, an original license or a renewal.

question.text: If you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision standard, what follows?

answer.text: If you need glasses or contacts to meet the vision standard, you must wear them every time you drive, and your license will carry a corrective-lens restriction.

teaching.text: If lenses got you through the vision check, wear them on every drive; your license will show the restriction. Remember: lenses on, every drive.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you need glasses or contacts to meet the vision standard, you must wear them every time you drive, and your license will carry a corrective-lens restriction.

question.text: How is driving without the corrective lenses your license requires punished?

answer.text: Driving without the corrective lenses your license requires is punished the same way as driving with no license at all.

teaching.text: Leaving required lenses off carries the same punishment as driving with no license. Remember: no lenses, no license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving without the corrective lenses your license requires is punished the same way as driving with no license at all.

question.text: Is breaking a corrective-lens restriction treated as a minor equipment fault?

answer.text: A corrective-lens restriction is not a suggestion: driving without the required lenses is treated like driving unlicensed, not like a minor equipment fault.

teaching.text: The restriction is binding, so ignoring it is treated as driving unlicensed, not as a small equipment slip. Remember: treated as unlicensed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A corrective-lens restriction is not a suggestion: driving without the required lenses is treated like driving unlicensed, not like a minor equipment fault.

question.text: When may a mental or physical condition lead to a denied or restricted license?

answer.text: A person whose mental or physical condition could make driving unsafe may be denied a license, while a person with a disability can get a restricted license if the condition does not prevent safe driving.

teaching.text: A condition that could make driving unsafe may lead to denial, but a disability that does not prevent safe driving can mean a restricted license. Remember: safety decides, not diagnosis.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A person whose mental or physical condition could make driving unsafe may be denied a license, while a person with a disability can get a restricted license if the condition does not prevent safe driving.

question.text: Does having a disability automatically keep a person from being licensed?

answer.text: A disability does not automatically bar licensing: the deciding question is whether the condition keeps the person from driving safely, and a restricted license is possible when it does not.

teaching.text: The question is always whether the person can drive safely, and a restricted license is possible when they can. Remember: can they drive safely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A disability does not automatically bar licensing: the deciding question is whether the condition keeps the person from driving safely, and a restricted license is possible when it does not.

question.text: Where does the on-road driving test fall in the testing order, and when is it required?

answer.text: The on-road driving test comes last, after every other test is passed; it is required for a first license, may be required at renewal, and is never required for a learner permit.

teaching.text: The road test is the final step after every other test; it is required for a first license, possible at renewal, and never needed for a permit. Remember: road test comes last.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The on-road driving test comes last, after every other test is passed; it is required for a first license, may be required at renewal, and is never required for a learner permit.

question.text: Is the road test required for a learner permit, a first license, or a renewal?

answer.text: The road test is the final step for a first license, but it is not required for a learner permit, and it may or may not be required at renewal.

teaching.text: For a permit the road test is never required, for a first license it is, and at renewal it may or may not be. Remember: first yes, permit never.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The road test is the final step for a first license, but it is not required for a learner permit, and it may or may not be required at renewal.

question.text: Must an original license applicant take the on-road test?

answer.text: Original license applicants must take the on-road test, although the handbook notes some cases where it may not be required.

teaching.text: Original license applicants take the on-road test, apart from some cases the handbook notes. Remember: new license, road test.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Original license applicants must take the on-road test, although the handbook notes some cases where it may not be required.

question.text: What do you demonstrate during the road test?

answer.text: During the road test you show that you can perform basic driving patterns and drive safely in traffic.

teaching.text: You show basic driving patterns and safe driving in real traffic. Remember: patterns and safe traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During the road test you show that you can perform basic driving patterns and drive safely in traffic.

question.text: What kinds of driving do road-test examiners grade?

answer.text: Road-test examiners grade how you approach intersections, stop signs and signals; quick stops on command; backing; stopping, starting and parking; clutch use in a manual car; turn signals and horn; turning; lane use; following; passing and being passed; yielding to pedestrians and vehicles; posture; and the three-point turnabout.

teaching.text: Examiners watch intersections, stops, backing, parking, signals, turning, lane use, following, passing, yielding, posture and the turnabout. Remember: every move is graded.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Road-test examiners grade how you approach intersections, stop signs and signals; quick stops on command; backing; stopping, starting and parking; clutch use in a manual car; turn signals and horn; turning; lane use; following; passing and being passed; yielding to pedestrians and vehicles; posture; and the three-point turnabout.

question.text: What vehicle must you use for your driving skills test?

answer.text: You must take the driving skills test in a vehicle that represents the license class you are applying for.

teaching.text: The test vehicle must represent the license class you are applying for. Remember: test in your class.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must take the driving skills test in a vehicle that represents the license class you are applying for.

question.text: How does the first step of a three-point turnabout begin and end?

answer.text: Three-point turnabout, step one: from the far right edge of the road, check for traffic, signal left, creep forward turning the wheel left, and stop several inches from the left curb or edge.

teaching.text: From the far right edge, check traffic, signal left, creep forward with the wheel turned left, and stop several inches short of the left curb. Remember: signal left, creep left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Three-point turnabout, step one: from the far right edge of the road, check for traffic, signal left, creep forward turning the wheel left, and stop several inches from the left curb or edge.

question.text: What do you do in the second step of a three-point turnabout?

answer.text: Three-point turnabout, step two: back up slowly while turning the wheel right, and stop several inches from the right curb or edge.

teaching.text: Back up slowly with the wheel turned right, and stop several inches from the right curb or edge. Remember: back up turning right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Three-point turnabout, step two: back up slowly while turning the wheel right, and stop several inches from the right curb or edge.

question.text: How do you finish a three-point turnabout?

answer.text: Three-point turnabout, step three: move forward slowly with the wheel turned left to complete the turnabout.

teaching.text: Pull forward slowly with the wheel turned left, and the turnabout is complete. Remember: forward, wheel left, done.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Three-point turnabout, step three: move forward slowly with the wheel turned left to complete the turnabout.

question.text: Which way does the wheel turn on each move of a three-point turnabout?

answer.text: In the three-point turnabout the wheel goes left on both forward moves and right on the backward move.

teaching.text: Both forward moves turn the wheel left, and the single backing move turns it right. Remember: left, right, left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In the three-point turnabout the wheel goes left on both forward moves and right on the backward move.

question.text: What decides whether you need a regular or a commercial license class?

answer.text: North Carolina issues both a regular driver license and a commercial driver license, and the vehicle you will drive decides which class you need.

teaching.text: North Carolina issues regular and commercial licenses, and the vehicle you will drive sets the class. Remember: the vehicle decides.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: North Carolina issues both a regular driver license and a commercial driver license, and the vehicle you will drive decides which class you need.

question.text: Which license class do most people need for personal cars and small trucks?

answer.text: Most drivers only need a regular Class C license for personal cars and small trucks.

teaching.text: Personal cars and small trucks need only a regular Class C license. Remember: most drivers carry Class C.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Most drivers only need a regular Class C license for personal cars and small trucks.

question.text: What vehicles does a regular Class C license cover?

answer.text: A regular Class C license covers a noncommercial single vehicle rated under twenty-six thousand one pounds, and a towing combination rated under twenty-six thousand one pounds combined when the driver is at least eighteen.

teaching.text: A regular Class C covers noncommercial single vehicles and towing combinations rated under twenty-six thousand and one pounds, towing once you are eighteen. Remember: under the big weight line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A regular Class C license covers a noncommercial single vehicle rated under twenty-six thousand one pounds, and a towing combination rated under twenty-six thousand one pounds combined when the driver is at least eighteen.

question.text: Regular and commercial licenses both use the letters A, B and C. Which one is the ordinary car license?

answer.text: Regular license classes and commercial license classes share the letters A, B and C, but a regular Class C is the ordinary noncommercial license that most car and small-truck drivers need.

teaching.text: The letters repeat across regular and commercial licenses, but the regular Class C is the ordinary noncommercial license. Remember: regular C is everyday.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Regular license classes and commercial license classes share the letters A, B and C, but a regular Class C is the ordinary noncommercial license that most car and small-truck drivers need.

question.text: What vehicle combination calls for a regular Class A license?

answer.text: A regular Class A license covers a CDL-exempt vehicle combination whose towed unit has a gross vehicle weight rating of ten thousand one pounds or more.

teaching.text: A CDL-exempt combination whose towed unit is rated ten thousand and one pounds or more calls for a regular Class A. Remember: heavy trailer means A.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A regular Class A license covers a CDL-exempt vehicle combination whose towed unit has a gross vehicle weight rating of ten thousand one pounds or more.

question.text: What single vehicle calls for a regular Class B license?

answer.text: A regular Class B license covers a CDL-exempt single vehicle rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, including when it tows a vehicle rated no more than ten thousand pounds.

teaching.text: A CDL-exempt single vehicle rated twenty-six thousand and one pounds or more calls for a regular Class B, even towing something light. Remember: heavy single vehicle means B.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A regular Class B license covers a CDL-exempt single vehicle rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, including when it tows a vehicle rated no more than ten thousand pounds.

question.text: What does the regular Class A threshold measure, compared with the Class B threshold?

answer.text: The regular Class A threshold is about the towed unit, rated ten thousand one pounds or more, while the regular Class B threshold is about a single vehicle rated twenty-six thousand one pounds or more.

teaching.text: Class A looks at the heavy towed unit, while Class B looks at the heavy single vehicle. Remember: A tows, B is heavy.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The regular Class A threshold is about the towed unit, rated ten thousand one pounds or more, while the regular Class B threshold is about a single vehicle rated twenty-six thousand one pounds or more.

question.text: Which handbooks do commercial and motorcycle applicants study?

answer.text: CDL Class A, B or C applicants study the CDL Handbook, and motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle permit applicants study the Motorcycle Handbook.

teaching.text: Commercial applicants study the CDL Handbook, and motorcycle applicants study the Motorcycle Handbook. Remember: CDL book, motorcycle book.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: CDL Class A, B or C applicants study the CDL Handbook, and motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle permit applicants study the Motorcycle Handbook.

question.text: Who must hold a commercial driver license?

answer.text: A commercial driver license is required for paid or volunteer drivers of the listed vehicle types that are built or used to carry passengers or property.

teaching.text: Paid or volunteer, a driver of the listed passenger or property vehicles needs a commercial license. Remember: paid or volunteer, still CDL.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A commercial driver license is required for paid or volunteer drivers of the listed vehicle types that are built or used to carry passengers or property.

question.text: What makes a vehicle a commercial Class A vehicle?

answer.text: A commercial Class A vehicle is a combination with a combined weight rating of at least twenty-six thousand one pounds whose towed unit is rated at least ten thousand one pounds.

teaching.text: A commercial Class A is a heavy combination whose towed unit is rated ten thousand and one pounds or more. Remember: heavy combo, heavy trailer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A commercial Class A vehicle is a combination with a combined weight rating of at least twenty-six thousand one pounds whose towed unit is rated at least ten thousand one pounds.

question.text: What makes a vehicle a commercial Class B vehicle?

answer.text: A commercial Class B vehicle is a single vehicle rated at least twenty-six thousand one pounds, or a combination whose towing unit is rated at least twenty-six thousand one pounds while the towed unit is rated under ten thousand one pounds.

teaching.text: A commercial Class B is a heavy single vehicle, or a heavy towing unit pulling a towed unit under ten thousand and one pounds. Remember: heavy truck, light trailer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A commercial Class B vehicle is a single vehicle rated at least twenty-six thousand one pounds, or a combination whose towing unit is rated at least twenty-six thousand one pounds while the towed unit is rated under ten thousand one pounds.

question.text: What makes a vehicle a commercial Class C vehicle?

answer.text: A commercial Class C vehicle is one outside Classes A and B that is built to carry sixteen or more people counting the driver, or that carries hazardous materials requiring placards.

teaching.text: Outside Classes A and B, a vehicle built for sixteen or more people counting the driver, or carrying placarded hazardous materials, is commercial Class C. Remember: riders or placards.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A commercial Class C vehicle is one outside Classes A and B that is built to carry sixteen or more people counting the driver, or that carries hazardous materials requiring placards.

question.text: Is a commercial Class C vehicle defined mainly by its weight?

answer.text: A commercial Class C vehicle is defined by what it carries, sixteen or more people counting the driver or placarded hazardous materials, not by weight alone.

teaching.text: Commercial Class C turns on passengers or placarded hazardous materials, not on weight alone. Remember: what it carries counts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A commercial Class C vehicle is defined by what it carries, sixteen or more people counting the driver or placarded hazardous materials, not by weight alone.

question.text: Which vehicles need no commercial license, and what license is still required?

answer.text: No CDL is needed for recreational vehicles, military equipment, fire or emergency equipment, or certain farm vehicles, but a regular license of the right class is always required.

teaching.text: Recreational, military, emergency and certain farm vehicles need no CDL, but always a regular license of the right class. Remember: no CDL, still licensed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No CDL is needed for recreational vehicles, military equipment, fire or emergency equipment, or certain farm vehicles, but a regular license of the right class is always required.

question.text: What license may an on-duty volunteer firefighter or EMS member use to drive emergency vehicles?

answer.text: On-duty volunteer fire, rescue or EMS members may drive Class A, B or C fire-fighting, rescue or EMS vehicles while holding only a regular A, B or C license.

teaching.text: On-duty volunteer fire, rescue or EMS members may drive those vehicles on a regular license of the matching class. Remember: volunteers drive on regular.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On-duty volunteer fire, rescue or EMS members may drive Class A, B or C fire-fighting, rescue or EMS vehicles while holding only a regular A, B or C license.

question.text: Which kinds of commercial driving each need a special endorsement?

answer.text: Hauling hazardous materials, carrying passengers, driving school or activity buses, pulling double trailers and driving tank vehicles each require a special CDL endorsement.

teaching.text: Hazardous materials, passengers, school or activity buses, double trailers and tank vehicles each need a special endorsement. Remember: special loads, special endorsement.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hauling hazardous materials, carrying passengers, driving school or activity buses, pulling double trailers and driving tank vehicles each require a special CDL endorsement.

question.text: What are the legal ways to operate a motorcycle on public roads?

answer.text: To operate a motorcycle on public roads, a person needs a motorcycle learner permit or a regular or commercial license carrying a motorcycle endorsement.

teaching.text: Ride on public roads with a motorcycle learner permit, or with a license that carries a motorcycle endorsement. Remember: permit or endorsement.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To operate a motorcycle on public roads, a person needs a motorcycle learner permit or a regular or commercial license carrying a motorcycle endorsement.

question.text: What must a motorcycle learner permit applicant already have, by age?

answer.text: A motorcycle learner permit applicant aged sixteen to seventeen must already hold a full provisional license and have a parent or guardian sign; an applicant eighteen or older must already hold a license from the division.

teaching.text: At sixteen or seventeen you need a full provisional license and a parent or guardian signature; at eighteen or older, a license from the division. Remember: teens need provisional plus parent.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A motorcycle learner permit applicant aged sixteen to seventeen must already hold a full provisional license and have a parent or guardian sign; an applicant eighteen or older must already hold a license from the division.

question.text: How is a motorcycle endorsement different from a motorcycle learner permit?

answer.text: A motorcycle endorsement is added to an existing regular or commercial license, while a motorcycle learner permit is a separate permit; either one allows motorcycle operation on public roads.

teaching.text: The endorsement is added to a license you hold, while the learner permit is its own separate permit. Remember: endorsement adds, permit stands alone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A motorcycle endorsement is added to an existing regular or commercial license, while a motorcycle learner permit is a separate permit; either one allows motorcycle operation on public roads.

question.text: What does a school bus driver need, and how do activity bus drivers differ?

answer.text: A school bus driver must be at least eighteen, have at least six months of driving experience, and hold a Class B or C CDL with S and P endorsements plus a School Bus Driver's Certificate; activity bus drivers meet the same terms without the certificate.

teaching.text: A school bus driver is at least eighteen, has six months of experience, holds a Class B or C CDL with S and P endorsements, and has the certificate. Remember: school bus needs certificate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A school bus driver must be at least eighteen, have at least six months of driving experience, and hold a Class B or C CDL with S and P endorsements plus a School Bus Driver's Certificate; activity bus drivers meet the same terms without the certificate.

question.text: What separates a school bus driver's requirements from an activity bus driver's?

answer.text: A school bus driver needs a School Bus Driver's Certificate on top of the CDL endorsements, while a school activity bus driver meets the same requirements without that certificate.

teaching.text: Activity bus drivers meet the same terms, but only the school bus driver needs the certificate. Remember: certificate is the difference.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A school bus driver needs a School Bus Driver's Certificate on top of the CDL endorsements, while a school activity bus driver meets the same requirements without that certificate.

question.text: Who can never get a commercial license with a passenger or school bus endorsement?

answer.text: Under G.S. twenty-thirty-seven.14A, the division will not issue or renew a CDL with a P or S endorsement for anyone who must register as a sex offender.

teaching.text: Anyone required to register as a sex offender cannot be issued or renew a CDL with a P or S endorsement. Remember: registered offenders barred.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under G.S. twenty-thirty-seven.14A, the division will not issue or renew a CDL with a P or S endorsement for anyone who must register as a sex offender.
